data: This page describes the design. Where a part is not written yet it says planned.
data.the-command-line-wctr#The command line,: The client. It finds the daemon at /var/run/wctr.sock, or at the address in the WCTR_HOST environment variable. Because the API is Docker-Engine compatible, other clients of that API can talk to wctrd as well; wctr is the command the labs teach.
data.the-daemon-wctrd#The daemon, wctrd: A Go program, pure Go, no cgo. It owns the images, the containers and their state, and serves an HTTP API on the Unix socket /var/run/wctr.sock. The API is compatible with the Docker Engine API: the reference it is written against is Docker Engine API v1.47, and the subset M1 covers is the one the commands pull, run, ps, logs, rm, rmi, inspect and images need: GET /_ping, POST /images/create, the image list and delete endpoints, and the container create, start, list, inspect, logs, wait and delete endpoints. Logs of a container without a TTY use the API’s multiplexed stream framing.
data.the-executors#The executors:
An executor runs one module with a root filesystem, arguments, an environment and a working directory.
wazero (M1, in progress): the native executor. wazero is a pure-Go WebAssembly runtime with a WASI preview1 implementation, so the engine stays a single static binary. The container’s root filesystem is adapted to wazero’s writable filesystem interface; the image’s WorkingDir is passed as PWD, which is where a Go wasip1 program takes its initial directory from. Browser worker (planned): the same executor contract implemented over the browser’s WebAssembly, in a Web Worker, so the playground needs no server that runs containers.
data.the-images#The images:
An image is an OCI image whose manifest or index entry has os=wasip1 and arch=wasm. The engine pulls from an OCI registry (the Distribution API, with the registry’s bearer-token authentication), selects the wasip1/wasm entry of an index, verifies digests, and unpacks the layers in order — whiteouts included — into the container’s root filesystem. The Wasm OCI artifact layout of the CNCF TAG-Runtime (application/wasm layer, application/vnd.wasm.config.v0+json config) is also read.
Images are meant to be apt-like: a small base plus the tools a lab needs, built from pkgx wasip1 bottles. go-pkgx is gaining a wasip1/wasm target for this; until it ships, images come from whatever registry holds wasip1 images.
data.the-pieces#The pieces: wctr CLI ──► /var/run/wctr.sock ──► wctrd ──► executor ──► a wasip1 module (Docker Engine API) │ │ │ ├─ native: wazero (M1, in progress) │ └─ browser worker (planned) └─ image store, root filesystem
data.what-is-not-in-this-design-yet#What is n: Networking (the WasmEdge socket ABI), wctr exec and a shell (a WASIX subset), building an image from a Dockerfile, Compose and a mini-Kubernetes are on the roadmap; none of them exists.

data.does-anything-work-with-existing-docker-: The API is meant to be compatible with the Docker Engine API (v1.47 is the reference the code is written against), so a client of that API can be pointed at /var/run/wctr.sock. Only the subset M1 needs is planned first; see the roadmap.
data.not-ctr#Not ctr: ctr is the command line that containerd ships. Trainees meet it on Kubernetes nodes, where it means something different, so a lab teaching a ctr of its own would teach the wrong tool in the place they will use it.
data.not-docker#Not docker: Docker is a product and a trademark of another organisation. This engine is not Docker and does not ship under its name: it is compatible with the Docker Engine API, which is a statement of compatibility and nothing more. That is why its socket is /var/run/wctr.sock and the address variable is WCTR_HOST.
data.why-wctr#Why wctr?: wctr is the command line and wctrd the daemon that serves it. The name follows the convention of the container tools that came before it, ctr, nerdctl and crictl: a short name ending in ctr, for container. The w is for wasm: wctr reads as wasm container, and says that this is the WebAssembly variant.

data: There is nothing to install yet. The engine has no release and no command to run: its image and root-filesystem packages are being written. This page says what M1 will let you do, and is updated when it does.
data.building-from-source-today#Building from:
The engine is a Go module that needs Go 1.27.3 or later:
git clone https://github.com/go-wasmcontainers/engine cd engine go build ./... That compiles the packages; there is no wctrd or wctr command to start until the daemon and its API are written.
data.the-session-m1-is-written-to-serve#The s:
Planned for M1 (native, wazero executor). Once wctrd is running and listening on /var/run/wctr.sock, wctr finds it by itself; WCTR_HOST points it elsewhere:
wctr pull # an OCI image with os=wasip1, arch=wasm wctr run # runs the module under wazero wctr ps # lists the containers wctr logs # its standard output and error wctr inspect # its configuration and state wctr images # lists the pulled images wctr rm wctr rmi Anything else (wctr exec, building an image, Compose, published ports) is planned, not part of M1; see the roadmap.
data.where-to-follow-it#Where to follow it: The engine’s progress is in go-wasmcontainers/engine; the page you are reading describes its main branch.

data:
Every behaviour of the engine that follows an external format or protocol is written against one of the documents below. The engine repository’s own docs/REFERENCES.md says, for each, which version was opened and which file it governs.
Reference What it decides OCI Image Format Specification (v1.1.1) digests, manifests, image indexes, image config, layers and whiteouts, image layout OCI Distribution Specification pulling manifests and blobs from a registry Docker Registry token authentication the bearer-token challenge and token request Docker Engine API (v1.47) the endpoints and schemas wctrd is compatible with Wasm OCI artifact layout (CNCF TAG-Runtime) media types and config fields of a Wasm image wazero (v1.12.0) the runtime, its WASI preview1 imports and writable filesystem interface WASI preview1 the system interface a wasip1 module is written against
Nothing on this page has shipped. It is the list of what the engine will not do on day one, so nobody has to guess.
data.in-progress#In progress: Item Status Engine M1: native, wazero executor; wctr pull, run, ps, logs, rm, rmi, inspect, images in progress
data.planned#Planned: Item What it is Browser executor the executor contract in a browser Web Worker, which the playground needs Playground an in-browser terminal running wctr against WASI containers, for cloud and container training labs (the playground repository exists; no code yet) Networking containers that listen and connect, through the WasmEdge socket ABI Shell and exec wctr exec and an interactive shell, through a WASIX subset Image build building an image from a Dockerfile Compose several containers described in one file Mini-Kubernetes enough of the orchestrator’s API to teach its concepts apt-like images a base image plus tools, from pkgx wasip1 bottles, once go-pkgx has its wasip1/wasm target An item moves to “in progress” when its code is on a branch, and is removed from this page when it ships, with the release that carries it.
